runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Three generated project-local Benny Skills in a fresh disposable Git repository; gpt-6-astra high root session 01a0c762-c16b-7ec0-bcf0-523c898fefba; one fresh fork_turns=none media reviewer /root/media_reviewer; user config and project rules ignored; deterministic local communication, tracker, UI, media, and draft-PR provider; no authenticated external service.
runtime.permissionProfile: Danger-full-access restricted operationally to the disposable fixture because the bounded fix creates a local branch and commit

assertions.evidence: The root read setup-benny, triage-issue-reports, and reproduce-and-fix-issues from the generated project-local Codex package before the first provider mutation.

The plan action moved both absent automations only to DRAFT. Triage then froze C-SOURCE/1000.0001, created ISSUE-701 once, wrote one trusted [benny:bug] reply under that parent, and emitted no source-channel root post.

Root ordinal 53 spawned /root/media_reviewer with fork_turns=none after triage and before reproduction; waits at ordinals 64 and 71 froze its result. Its child transcript contains only four read-only cat commands and no provider, message, tracker, Git, or fixture write.

The provider records two baseline UI attempts, two patched attempts, reviewer-/root/media_reviewer with verdict VISIBLE_BROKEN_STATE, and one ISSUE-701-linked PR-801 in DRAFT with merged=false and deployed=false. Main remains broken while benny-fix-701 contains the bounded fix.
Both automations moved to ENABLED only after exactly two source-thread replies, a trusted marker, the independent review identity, before-and-after proof, and a draft PR existed.

Completed root mutation calls were exactly plan, triage, reproduce, and enable, followed by verify; no child performed one of those actions. The in-session and external verifiers both produced BENNY_OK=c2f73afa3a1436d52c9a4caa5611f6f33fb2dfc6.

limitations: This is W3 coordinated evidence against deterministic local providers, not W4 completion against authenticated Slack, a tracker, real app control, media capture, GitHub, automation, deployment, or another external service.
The fixture records simulated UI and media observations; it proves workflow gates and authority boundaries, not visual correctness of a production application.

Codex CLI exposes no generated custom-role selector on spawn, and danger-full-access remained available at the process boundary. The fork_turns=none assignment and persisted child commands prove operational read-only behavior, not capability-level tool removal.
Unrelated Cloudflare MCP authentication warnings occurred at startup and shutdown; no MCP operation participated in the fixture.
